AUDIT: PASS
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'Extend deterministic report to cover PR merge state and PM own dispatch tracking, close the last manual-query gaps' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  PROGRESS.md                   | 137 ++++++++++++------------
 TRACKED_PRS.json              |   1 +
 generate_pm_report_v3.py      | 235 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-
 test_generate_pm_report_v3.py | 182 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 489 insertions(+), 66 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: This is a clean, well-architected additive change to generate_pm_report_v3.py: two new deterministic, zero-AI-call sections (16: tracked-PR merge state via list-form `gh pr view` subprocess calls against a real, configurable, file-backed JSON list with honest missing/malformed-config handling; 17: per-row recent owner-dispatched UMR status via a parameterized SQL query) that reuse existing helpers/constants (run_cmd, GH_ORG, OWNER_DISPATCH_SOURCE_TRIGGER, _age_hours_since, sbr._connect) rather than duplicating them, follow the file's established honest-error/no-fabrication conventions, and ship with 13 new unit tests covering missing/malformed config, gh success/failure, windowing, and graceful degradation on schema mismatch; I ran the full suite myself (not just trusting the self-report) and independently confirmed 115 passed / 1 pre-existing failure (test_end_to_end_smoke_run, an unrelated gtm_test_script_build_check.py fixture-mocking gap not touched by this diff). No .github/workflows/** changes, no migrations/schema/auth/payment/security path matches, so the tier1 classification is correct, and there is no command-injection or credential-handling concern since all `gh` calls use list-form argv with no shell. The one real caveat, verified independently with a read-only `git merge-tree` simulation rather than assumed: PR #198 currently shows GitHub mergeable=CONFLICTING/mergeStateStatus=DIRTY against main, but the conflict is confined entirely to PROGRESS.md (a shared running-log file every worker task rewrites, with an established repo convention of keeping the branch's own content) -- generate_pm_report_v3.py, TRACKED_PRS.json, and test_generate_pm_report_v3.py all merge cleanly with zero conflicts, so this is a mechanical docs-merge issue, not a code defect, but it does mean an autonomous `gh pr merge` will fail until PROGRESS.md is rebased/resolved. Issues found: PR #198 is currently GitHub mergeable=CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus=DIRTY against main (verified via `gh pr view` and a read-only `git merge-tree` simulation). The conflict is isolated to PROGRESS.md (routine shared-log collision with PR #197, which merged into main after this branch's base) -- all code/test/config files merge cleanly. An autonomous `gh pr merge` will fail as-is; PROGRESS.md needs a rebase/resolve (keep this branch's own Completed/Remaining content, per this repo's established convention) before merge can actually succeed.; Minor: in get_recent_owner_umr_status_section(), if conn.execute() raises sqlite3.Error, the already-open `conn` is never closed (the close() call only runs on the success path) -- a low-severity connection/resource leak on the error path, not a functional bug since sqlite connections are eventually reclaimed, but worth a follow-up try/finally.
Severity Classified: none
Verdict: pass
Corrective Action Owner: Not required -- no issues found in this review.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Not required -- approved as-is, no follow-up needed.

Evidence Recorded: This is a clean, additive change to generate_pm_report_v3.py that adds two new deterministic report sections (tracked-PR merge state via `gh pr view` over a real, file-backed, env-overridable config list, and recent owner-dispatched UMR status via a parameterized SQL query), plus a shipped-empty TRACKED_PRS.json config file, updated module docstring/version bump, and 13 new unit tests; it touches no migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths and no .github/workflows/** files, matching its tier1 classification. I ran the real test suite myself rather than trusting the self-report: 115 passed / 1 failed after this diff, and confirmed by checking out the base commit that the same single failure (test_end_to_end_smoke_run, an unrelated pre-existing gtm_test_script_build_check.py monkeypatch gap) was already failing before this diff (103 passed / 1 failed), so the claim of a pre-existing, unrelated failure holds up.
